Paper: Genomic signatures of homologous recombination deficiency predict response to PARP inhibition in chordoma
review_status: Newly available 2026-09-10; locally present but absent from the original 69-row matrix
N: 11 patients; WES for 9 and WGS for 2, with matched blood
Assay: Matched tumor-normal whole-exome or whole-genome sequencing
Input_datatype: Somatic mutations and allele-aware copy-number states
Ground_truth_HRD_definition: Mutational signature 3 plus genomic scars and clinical PARP-inhibitor response
HRD_calculation_method: LOH and LST-like measures; no methylation-derived canonical HRDsum
LOH_definition: Copy-neutral and non-copy-neutral LOH regions greater than 15 Mb; whole-chromosome handling follows the study implementation
LST_definition: Breaks between segments greater than 10 Mb after filtering small segments
Upstream_allele_specific_CN_method: Matched tumor-normal WES/WGS allele-specific copy-number analysis
Purity_ploidy_correction: Not reported in sufficient detail in the reviewed main article
CNV_method: Allele-aware sequencing CN with matched normal
Raw_IDAT_MU_requirement: No methylation-array input; matched sequencing required
Calibration_uncertainty: No predictive calibration or individual interval; descriptive rare-cohort evidence
Validation_strategy: Cohort survey plus olaparib response and acquired resistance
Performance_metrics: Descriptive genomic prevalence and clinical response
Single_sample_compatible: Sequencing is sample-level; no methylation predictor
Major_strengths: Matched-normal sequencing and clinically linked HRD evidence in a rare tumor
Major_limitations: Very small cohort and no methylation array
Direct_relevance_KIDS26: Rare-cancer motivation while reinforcing allele-aware reference labels
Implementation_ideas: Preserve component labels and do not infer allelic imbalance from total CN
documented_fact: Eleven advanced chordomas had matched tumor-normal sequencing; LOH regions exceeded 15 Mb and LST counted breaks between segments exceeding 10 Mb after small-segment filtering.
inference: Rare-tumor relevance does not validate methylation-derived canonical HRDsum.
recommendation: Use as biological motivation, not as evidence to change the primary model.
